title: David Valadao discusses crop protection and olive oil standards on social media - Kern County Times
text:
U.S. Representative David Valadao, who represents California’s 22nd district in Congress, posted a series of tweets on January 14, 2026, highlighting his recent efforts related to agriculture and food industry standards in the Central Valley.
In one post from January 14, Valadao stated, “I just met with the California Apple Commission to discuss pest and disease control research funding. Protecting the Valley’s specialty crops from disease-carrying pests is a critical step in supporting our producers, and I look forward to continuing this important conversation.”
Later that day, Valadao addressed issues surrounding olive oil production and labeling standards. In a tweet posted at 22:18 UTC, he wrote, “By establishing these standards, we can protect consumers from misleading labeling, promote transparency in the marketplace, and ensure a level playing field for our domestic olive oil producers.” He included a link for readers to access further information.
He also announced legislative action in collaboration with another lawmaker: “The Central Valley is one of the nation’s leading regions for olive oil production, and as demand grows, it’s important industry standards can keep up. That’s why I’m proud to join @RepJoshHarder to introduce the Olive Oil Standards Act.”
Valadao has served as U.S. Representative for California’s 22nd District since 2021 after previously serving in the California State Assembly from 2010 to 2012. He was born in Hanford, California in 1977 and continues to reside there.
